## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Restore the five-attempt cap before merge to limit request load during an outage. Retry truncated HTTP responses so a premature disconnect can recover within the configured attempts.

## Changes

The pull request adds `fetch_with_retry` with a configurable delay and up to ten attempts. It updates the written retry cap and adds retry tests and a review fixture.

## Critical

- app/net.py:19 — correctness — Enforce the five-attempt cap — When an upstream keeps raising `OSError`, the default call attempts the request ten times, and validation accepts explicit counts from six through ten. `AGENTS.md:5` requires “Retry helpers under app/ must cap attempts at 5.” — During an outage, each default call can send five extra requests to the failing upstream and delay error delivery.

## Important

- app/net.py:24 — correctness — Retry truncated HTTP responses — When a server closes the connection before sending the full `Content-Length` body, `fetch` raises `http.client.IncompleteRead` on the first attempt. The `except OSError` handler lets that exception escape even when attempts remain. — Callers receive an error after a truncated response even if a second request would return the complete body.
